verdict.rationale: Neon documents its own restore capability: an 'Instant restore' docs page, branch restore that moves compute endpoints to a new branch without changing the connection string (`finalize_restore: true`), and MCP tools to restore branches and snapshots. The evidence never states restoring to an arbitrary point in time within a retention window; the documented restores are tied to branches and snapshots. missing for 10: explicit point-in-time (timestamp/LSN) restore documentation, retention-window definition, independent or hands-on corroboration of recovery from bad writes.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can restore or branch the database to any point in time within the retention window to recover from bad writes

citations.quote: restores them without changing the connection string, by transferring compute endpoints to a new branch via the `finalize_restore: true` flag
create/reset/restore branches, "Finalize branch restore from snapshot"
Restores allow platforms to move between versions instantly.
